speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my clinic. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to begin our evaluation, have you noticed any changes in your vision, such as blurred vision or diplopia, or any difficulty with swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for describing your ataxia; specifically, does this clumsiness worsen when you close your eyes or try to touch your nose with your finger? Additionally, have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs, or any changes in your bowel and bladder habits?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a crucial clue; given your history of Crohn's disease and recent initiation of natalizumab, I am concerned about the risk of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). Has your vision remained clear, and have you noticed any new cognitive changes like memory loss or difficulty speaking? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). Comments: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Patient
text: The walking difficulty and coordination problems are the main issues. I do not have chest pain or other major symptoms besides the neurological problems. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with contrast.
